comment: Per-device facts droidtop cannot ask Android for: the pad's USB identity, how many panels the device really has, and quirks worth naming. Every field here is read off the device; nothing is inferred from a spec sheet. Fields droidtop's controller detection reads (docs/SPEC.md 7b): match.model (ro.product.model, case-insensitive; match.manufacturer optional), gamepad.name/vendorId/productId (the built-in pad's identity), gamepad.glyphFamily (xbox, playstation or nintendo: what is printed on the face buttons), and layoutToggle {property, values{<value>: {keysSwapped, confirmOn: bottom|right}}} for a system setting that changes the layout at any time. A value not listed is unknown, never guessed.

retroid-pocket-5.name: Retroid Pocket 5

gamepad.name: Retroid Pocket Controller
gamepad.notes: The d-pad reports BOTH the hat axes and the BTN_DPAD_* keys, so a reader that consumes both sees every press twice.

retroid-pocket-5.source: Read from the console itself on 2026-09-10: /proc/bus/input/devices and `getevent -pl` for the pad, the running display mode for the panel.

0.note: Default. Xbox-style positions as printed on the pad.

1.note: The value the system button-layout toggle writes when the owner swapped it (2026-10-02). That it swaps the reported A/B and X/Y keycodes, so the right button reports BUTTON_A, is the expected meaning and still to be confirmed on the console.

layoutToggle.source: Property name and the two values read on the console itself on 2026-10-02 (ro.product.model=Retroid Pocket 5).
